text:
ash: Heads-up — we saw a 3-4x p99 token latency blip on us-west1 dedicated slices around 09:14 UTC. Suspect noisy neighbor KV-cache churn.
priya: saw that, digging logs now. latencyAlerter triggered, linked traces look like repeated KVCACHE_EVICTs.
mike: can you paste the eviction log snippet?
priya: sure, small excerpt: ```
[09:14:02] alloc=ded-slice-78 host=rack24-node3 KVCACHE_EVICT keys=125evicts dur=312ms
[09:14:03] alloc=ded-slice-78 host=rack24-node3 KVCACHE_EVICT keys=143evicts dur=298ms
[09:14:04] alloc=ded-slice-78 host=rack24-node3 THROTTLE_WAIT dur=120ms
```
sara: that pattern is classic noisy-host -> prefetch thrash. Dedicated slice was small (2xA10). We should consider a quarantine timer when we detect sustained evictions to stop routing similar requests to same host.
ash: proposal: add a quarantine backoff per host: initial 30s, exponential to 8m, reset after 30m idle. Also add a soft-credit for dedicated slices so they can borrow a small burst credit from regional pool rather than hot-spot a single host.
mike: i like credits — avoids immediate evict/reshuffle churn. what's the math? costs?
priya: rough calc: if we allow 5% of region pool as burst credits, worst-case extra spend ~ +2.5% on GPU hours for the region during peak. But we reduce oscillation and downstream SLO penalties.
sara: alternative is increase the quarantine to fixed 5m and force routing to a different az temporarily, but that increases egress and cross-az latency.
ash: tradeoffs noted. prefer backoff + local credit smoothing. ops impact: we need new metric (host_quarantine_count, credit_consumed) and dashboard.
mike: also need a safe fallback: if credits exhausted, route to lower-cost quantized model variant (quant8) for short time window rather than retrying same host. saves both latency and cost.
priya: agreed. I'll sketch a canary: rollout to us-west1 non-prod first, 2h canary. Metrics to watch: p99 gen latency, kvcache_eviction_rate, host_quarantine_rate, credit_utilization, cost_delta.
ash: can we implement the quarantine gating in router runtime without hot restart? i.e., config flag flip?
priya: yes — router reads dynamic policy from config store. we can ship low-risk change. need to add metric tags.
ash: assign: @priya implement router gate + metrics, @mike design credit pool algorithm and cost projection, @sara prepare runbook update and cross-az fallback logic. I can own canary coordination.
mike: will do cost projection by EOD. question: what threshold for sustained evictions to trigger quarantine? 3 evictions within 20s? 5 within 60s?
sara: suggestion: use eviction-rate rolling window: if evictions/sec > 2 for 30s and p95 gen latency > baseline*1.5 then quarantine. keeps noise false positives low.
priya: makes sense. I'll add that rule to the canary config.
deploy-bot: canary policy config pushed to us-west1-nonprod at 10:05 UTC :rocket:
infra-bot: alert rule created: host_quarantine_rate > 0 -> channel #eng-infra for visibility.
ash: ok plan sounds good. @mike please also include expected rollback criteria (cost > +5% sustained OR p99 not improved after 30m).
mike: noted. will share doc.
sara: scheduling 30m sync in 20m to confirm flags before canary. :calendar: 
ash: thanks all. if canary looks stable we'll stage to prod us-west1 with 2hr observation window. :thumbsup:
